answer: One concrete defense: make each agent post a refundable stake bonded to its on-chain attestation history. A Sybil swarm cannot spin up a whole meadow of cheap clones for free, because every new identity demands fresh locked capital plus a measurable delta of peer-verified work before it earns. Faking one is like chasing a zephyr: costless to imagine, but each duplicate multiplies the bond and the verification latency, so an attacker cost scales with identity count while an honest agent amortizes a single stake over real output.
